title: What Holds Clusters Together?
question: What are galaxy clusters made of, and why is most of their mass unseen?
hook: The part of a galaxy cluster we can see in a photograph is only a small slice of it.
idea: A galaxy cluster is mostly dark matter, with hot gas and a small share of galaxies.

beats.prompt: You add up the mass of the galaxies in a cluster, the only part visible in ordinary light. How does that compare with the cluster's total mass?

choices.label: Galaxies make up nearly all of it
choices.feedback: Tempting because galaxies are the only part we see in visible light, but they are only a small fraction.

choices.label: Galaxies are a small fraction, and dark matter is most of it
Hot gas makes up most of it
choices.feedback: Gas is a main component, but dark matter makes up the majority of the mass.

beats.explain: Galaxies make up a small fraction of a cluster, while dark matter makes up the majority of its mass.

beats.prompt: Match each part of a cluster to what is true of it.
pairs: The only part we can detect in visible light
Reaches 30 to 100 million degrees Celsius at its peak
Most of the mass, yet undetectable optically
beats.explain: A cluster has three main components, and only the galaxies show up in visible light.

beats.prompt: A cluster lies between us and a very distant, faint galaxy. What does the cluster do to that galaxy's light?

choices.label: Its gravity bends the light's path, magnifying the view
It blocks the light so the galaxy vanishes
choices.feedback: Tempting because the cluster is huge, but its gravity bends the path of photons rather than stopping them.

choices.label: It leaves the light untouched
choices.feedback: Near massive clusters, gravity distorts space-time and bends the path of photons.

beats.explain: Clusters act as gravitational lenses, bending photons into a cosmic magnifying glass that lets telescopes see distant galaxies.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: A galaxy cluster holds hundreds to thousands of galaxies bound by gravity.
Galaxies are the only part of a cluster we can see in visible light.
So the galaxies must make up most of a cluster's mass.
Therefore a cluster needs nothing we cannot see.
beats.explain: Being the only visible part does not make galaxies the main mass; dark matter makes up most of it.
